question: A and B are two students in a class. Their chances of solving a problem independently are 1/5 and 1/4 respectively. If both try to solve the problem independently, (a) what is the probability that the problem is solved? (b) If it is solved, what is the probability it was solved by B alone? (c) If the teacher finds that the problem was not solved by either A or B, what is the probability both failed to solve it?
explanation:
Let E1: A solves, P(E1)=1/5; E2: B solves,P(E2)=1/4; E1',E2': they fail.
They act independently.

(a) P(problem is solved)= 1 - P(both fail)
$=1 - P(E_1')P(E_2')$
$=1 - (1-1/5)(1-1/4)$
$=1 - (4/5)\times(3/4)=1-3/5=2/5$

(b) Probability solved by B alone = B solves and A does not:
$P(B\text{ alone})=P(E_1')P(E_2)= (4/5)\times(1/4)=1/5$
Given that problem is solved: $P(B\text{ alone}|\text{solved})=\dfrac{1/5}{2/5}=1/2$

(c) The teacher finds neither solved: Probability both failed = P(E1')P(E2') = $4/5 \times 3/4 = 3/5$
If teacher finds neither solved, certainty that both failed is 1 (given no outside solver), so probability is 1.

Final answers:
(a) $\dfrac{2}{5}$
(b) $\dfrac{1}{2}$
(c) $1$
